topic_tag: a salt mine and a city's art museum
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______.

worlds.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. Its chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, reached by a single lift. While the museum's building was rebuilt, its paintings went down in numbered crates and were set in an old spoil chamber. Once a month a curator rode down with a thermometer, checked each crate's seal against her list, and rode back up; the crates themselves never moved. When the new building opened, they came up in numbered order, and every canvas matched the photograph taken as it was packed.
worlds.explanation: "Depository" fits: while the museum had no building, its paintings sat sealed in crates that a curator checked but never opened or moved, and every canvas came back exactly as packed, so the mine held the collection safe until it was wanted again. "Gallery" fails because only a curator ever went down, and the crates stayed sealed and in place, so nothing was shown. "Hospital" fails because the curator's monthly care involved only checking the air and the seals, and every canvas came back matching its packing photograph, so nothing was treated. "Dump" fails because, although the crates sat in an old spoil chamber, every one came back up in order when the building opened.

gallery.inference: A gallery displays works to viewers; the only visitor was a curator checking seals once a month, and the crates never moved, so the paintings were held out of sight, not shown.

worlds.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. Its chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, reached by a single lift. The museum sent down the pictures it valued least, and they hung uncrated along the largest chamber's walls under electric lamps, each with a printed card beside it. A restorer rode down each morning to look them over, and on weekends the lift ran from noon to dusk while townspeople waited their turn on the miners' benches. When the museum's new building opened, every picture went back up as it had come down.
worlds.explanation: "Gallery" fits: the pictures hung on lit walls with printed cards, and townspeople queued every weekend to ride down and see them, so the mine was where the museum showed this part of its collection. "Depository" fails because the pictures were not packed away for safekeeping; they hung uncrated and the public came to look at them. "Hospital" fails because the restorer's daily visits were inspections: every picture went back up as it had come down, unrepaired. "Dump" fails because, although these were the museum's least valued pictures, they were labeled, displayed and all brought back up.

depository.why: The public came down to see the pictures.
depository.surface_fit: A museum moving pictures into a cool, dry mine for years and taking them all back sounds like safekeeping, so "depository" is the natural first guess.
depository.inference: A depository holds things away for safekeeping; these pictures hung uncrated under lamps with cards beside them while townspeople queued every weekend to see them, so the mine was showing them, not storing them.

worlds.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. Its chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, reached by a single lift. The museum sent down the paintings it had struck from its catalog, water-stained copies and works no buyer would take, and miners leaned them in rows along the walls of a worked-out chamber, which was then bricked up. The museum's inventory marks each of them destroyed, and the chamber has not been opened since.
worlds.explanation: "Dump" fits: the museum sent down works it had struck from its catalog and could not even sell, its inventory marks them destroyed, and the chamber was walled up and never reopened, so the mine was where it got rid of them. "Depository" fails because a depository keeps things for their owner to retrieve; these works had been struck from the catalog, so the museum no longer counted them as its own, and its inventory now marks them destroyed, so they were put away for good rather than held for later. "Hospital" fails because the water-stained copies were leaned against the walls and bricked in, with no one ever working on them. "Gallery" fails because, although the paintings were set out in rows along the walls, the chamber was bricked up at once and has stayed shut, so no one ever saw them.

depository.inference: A depository holds things its owner means to get back; these works had been struck from the museum's catalog, no buyer would take them, and the museum's own inventory records them as destroyed before the chamber was walled in, so the museum was disposing of them, not keeping them.

worlds.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. Its chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, reached by a single lift. After a flood soaked the museum, its water-stained paintings went down a few at a time and were laid uncrated on long tables in a lamp-lit chamber closed to the public, where restorers worked through them in turn. Each painting rode the lift back up within a year or two of arriving, its colors cleaned and its torn canvas patched, and the next damaged batch took its place on the tables.
worlds.explanation: "Hospital" fits: paintings arrived damaged, were laid out on restorers' tables and worked through, and left within a year or two cleaned and mended, with the next damaged batch coming in behind them, so the mine was where the museum's injured works were treated. "Depository" fails because the paintings were not put away to be kept: they were unpacked onto worktables and sent back once repaired, making room for the next batch. "Gallery" fails because the restorers' chamber was closed to the public. "Dump" fails because every painting rode the lift back up, repaired.

depository.inference: A depository keeps things packed away until they are wanted; these paintings were unpacked onto worktables, sent back as soon as the restorers finished, and replaced by the next damaged batch, so the chamber was a place of treatment, not storage.
